title: Dynamic SLO tiers and adaptive error-budget reallocation for multimodal inference
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We need an operationally safe way to map internal SLOs to customer-facing SLAs for multimodal endpoints (text+image) and to reallocate error budget dynamically across model variants during bursty traffic or partial degradation. Existing tickets cover static latency bands and staged deployments, but they do not address cross-variant error budget borrowing, or adaptive rollback thresholds for mixed-modality requests.

Scope: Define SLO bands (p50/p95/p99), uptime targets, and error budget accounting rules for multimodal inference. Define rules for dynamic error-budget reallocation across variants (e.g., full-precision vs quantized) and across routes (chat vs batch embeddings). Specify automated rollout gates and rollback triggers for canaries and ramping policies. Produce acceptance criteria, telemetry requirements, and customer-facing SLA mapping.

Out of scope: implementation details of kernel selection, deep runtime scheduling, and exact alert runbooks (those will be handled by ENG follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Define three operational SLO tiers for multimodal endpoints with clear p50/p95/p99 latency targets and expected throughput ranges.
Specify uptime SLO and corresponding monthly error budget per tier (e.g., 99.95% => 21.6 minutes/month).
Provide a deterministic formula for error-budget reallocation between model variants and routes, including a safety cap that prevents >20% budget transfer without manual approval.
Design rollout gates for canary -> ramp -> global with concrete thresholds on latency/p99 error rate/resource-saturation; each gate must include automated rollback conditions.
List the minimal telemetry signals required for automated gating (p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, GPU utilization, queue length, model fallback rate, KV cache hit rate).
Map internal SLO tiers to customer-facing SLA language for contract teams and sales (two sample SLA wording snippets).

Provide simulated examples (3 scenarios) showing how dynamic reallocation behaves during (a) sudden p95 regression in quantized variant, (b) regional outage with capacity shift, (c) bursty embedding workload affecting chat routes.
Specify dashboard and alert definitions required to operationalize gates and post-mortem templates when rollback happens.
decisions: Adopt three SLO tiers: gold (latency-sensitive), standard (balanced), and economy (cost-optimized).
Error-budget reallocation will be additive and time-bounded (max 20% of donor budget per 24h window) and require manual approval for transfers exceeding safety cap.
Rollout gates will be enforced by the control plane: canary window length = 30m, ramp steps = 10%, 25%, 50%, 100% with evaluation at each step.
Automated rollback triggers: sustained p99 degradation >25% vs baseline for 10 minutes OR 5xx rate above defined threshold for 5 minutes OR queue length growth >2x baseline for 15 minutes.
Customer SLA mapping: Gold => 99.9% uptime + p95 <= 300ms; Standard => 99.5% uptime + p95 <= 700ms; Economy => 99.0% uptime + p95 <= 1500ms. (Examples for negotiation only.)
open_questions: What is the canonical baseline window for p95/p99 comparisons (15m, 1h, or 24h)?
Should error-budget donations be directional only (from economy->standard) or bi-directional between any variants/routes?
Is a manual approval flow acceptable for >20% transfers, or should we provide an automated evacuation path with additional guardrails?
How do we account for multimodal requests that fan-out to multiple models (e.g., image encoder + text decoder)? How is budget charged/consumed across components?
